en: The Dyad on Having an Object of Refuge; The Triad on Internal Objects.

Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and having an internal object, there arises a state that is without-conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not having an internal object by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) and having an internal object, there arises a state that is without-conflict and not having an internal object by way of root condition.
[Under] root [condition] there are two; under mutuality (*aññamañña*) one ... pe ... under resultant (*vipāka*) one ... pe ... under non-disappearance (*avigata*) two.

Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and has an external object, there arises a state that is without-conflict (*nasaṇa*) and does not have an external object, by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) and has an external object, there arises a state that is without-conflict and does not have an external object, by way of root condition.
[Under] root [condition], there are two; under mutuality (*aññamañña*), one … pe … under resultant (*vipāka*), one … pe … under non-disappearance (*avigata*), two.
